proposed_comments.title: Dispose the selected tray bitmap on every path
proposed_comments.body:
### Dispose the selected tray bitmap on every path

**Severity:** `high`

`ChangeIcon` uses `Images.notify_default` when adaptive icons are disabled, but the current cleanup is conditional on `disposeBitmap`. Repeated normal tray updates therefore retain each bitmap-backed GDI object. Dispose the selected bitmap after creating the icon, while preserving the existing icon-handle ownership boundary.

```suggestion
bm.Dispose();
```

confidence.rationale: The default bitmap path leaves the selected bitmap undisposed. The one-line exact candidate and combined candidate both built successfully.

proposed_comments.title: Avoid the system-theme read when adaptive icons are disabled
proposed_comments.body:
### Avoid the system-theme read when adaptive icons are disabled

**Severity:** `medium`

The non-adaptive path still calls `GetSystemTheme()` only to compute `darkShell`, even though the drawing branches already use the fixed non-adaptive colors. Guard this registry read with `themeAdaptive` so disabling the feature does not perform unnecessary theme-service work on every icon refresh.

```suggestion
var darkShell = themeAdaptive && ManagedCommon.ThemeHelpers.GetSystemTheme() == ManagedCommon.AppTheme.Dark;
```

confidence.rationale: The non-adaptive branches use fixed colors, so the unconditional theme read is unnecessary. The exact one-line candidate and combined candidate both built successfully.

proposed_comments.title: Keep theme-adaptive fan-out scoped to implemented consumers
proposed_comments.body:
**Affected code:** `src/settings-ui/Settings.UI.Library/ThemeAdaptiveTrayIconFanOut.cs`, `ApplyToModules` and its module-specific helpers.

**Severity:** `high`

**Problem:** The new general setting writes and broadcasts `show_theme_adaptive_tray_icon` to Awake, ZoomIt, PowerDisplay, and Mouse Without Borders, but this change only proves the Mouse Without Borders consumer. A setting exposed as a cross-module master switch must either have a complete consumer and refresh path in every named module or be scoped to the modules implemented here; otherwise users can enable a setting that silently has no effect.

**Why it matters:** Users can see and enable a global setting while one or more named modules ignore it, leaving tray behavior inconsistent and making the setting contract misleading.

**Suggested change:**
1. Add and test the missing module readers and refresh paths, or remove the unsupported fan-out and adjust the setting text to the implemented module set.
2. In `ApplyToModules`, keep the invoked helpers aligned with consumers that deserialize and apply the property.
3. Toggle the setting for each named module and confirm every supported consumer changes its tray icon.

**Verification:** Build the exact upstream Settings and module projects, then perform the per-module toggle test. Confirm supported consumers refresh and unsupported modules are no longer advertised.
proposed_comments.out_of_diff_reason: The correction requires coordinated module consumers, refresh paths, and localized setting scope/text decisions across Settings.UI.Library and module implementations; no single current RIGHT-side range can safely apply the complete fix.
proposed_comments.outOfDiffReason: The correction requires coordinated module consumers, refresh paths, and localized setting scope/text decisions across Settings.UI.Library and module implementations; no single current RIGHT-side range can safely apply the complete fix.

confidence.rationale: ApplyToModules names four module consumers, but the current change does not establish a complete cross-module contract. This is intentionally retained as implementation-ready prose after extracting the two localized tray fixes.
